requirements.evidence: Contract is present and correct: enum cases (app/Enums/CallMode.php:7-9), RuntimeException subclass (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), and the exact invokable signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:35). Candidate filtering/ordering (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:114-134), any-mode fairness (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:49-51, 90-109), DB queue re-read under lock (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:40-47), candidate lock/re-check/skip (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:61-77), dedicated exception (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:53-55, 79) and immutable field update (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:71-76) all match the rules. Edge case missed: the fairness restriction is computed once, so if a concurrent Ticket::call() takes the only waiting normal after line 49, the skip loop empties the normal-only candidate list and line 79 throws even though priority tickets are still waiting.

conventions.evidence: Domain write lives in app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php (conventions.md:42-45), docs are kept in sync (docs/business-rules.md:103, docs/architecture.md:122-131) and CHANGELOG.md:20 was updated. Tests ship with the behavior (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php). One deviation: the new public __invoke (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:35) has no PHPDoc although conventions.md:102 requires PHPDoc on public methods touched, while both private helpers are documented (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:83-89, 111-113).

security.evidence: No client-controlled input or UI surface is introduced; the task explicitly makes the caller trusted and authorization out of scope (task.md:11-12, 64-67). Queue state is re-read from the database under a row lock rather than trusted from the instance (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:40-47), and only the three allowed ticket attributes are written explicitly (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:71-74), so mass assignment and stale-state attacks are avoided. No secrets, queries from user input, or unescaped output.

tests.evidence: Tests cover ordering and tie-breaks (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:246-281), queue isolation (283-301), both restricted modes (303-324), fairness and its reset/no-normal branches (326-401), inactive queue and stale instance (424-446), no-eligible exceptions (448-469) and the write-once fields (471-487). Missing coverage: the concurrent candidate-flip/skip branch required by rule 7 (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:61-77) is never exercised, and no test proves that calls made in priority_only/normal_only count in the fairness history or that other queues' calls are ignored.

simplicity.evidence: The action is small and reuses the existing Queue/Ticket models plus the existing InactiveQueueException (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:23-31), with no service layer or speculative abstractions. It does duplicate the state transition that Ticket::call() already provides (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:71-74 versus task.md:5-6), and the same `NormalOnly || restrictToNormal` predicate is repeated at app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:122 and 126.

readability.evidence: Focused methods with clear names (`fairnessTripped`, `candidateIds`), an easy-to-follow transaction body (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:35-80), explanatory comments for the stale-instance and exactly-once decisions (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:38-39, 57-60), and useful docblocks on both private helpers (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:83-89, 111-113). No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: All changed files serve the task: the action (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php), enum (app/Enums/CallMode.php), exception (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php), tests (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php), the two required docs (docs/business-rules.md, docs/architecture.md) and the conventional CHANGELOG.md entry. No unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: The fairness restriction and candidate list are computed once; if a concurrent Ticket::call() takes the only waiting normal before it is locked, the code skips it and line 79 throws NoWaitingTicketsException instead of falling back to priority tickets as rule 4 requires when no normal is waiting.
No test exercises the exactly-once skip path required by rule 7, where the chosen candidate is concurrently no longer waiting and the action must move to the next candidate.

Fairness tests seed only called tickets directly in the database; nothing verifies that calls made through priority_only/normal_only count in the history, and no test checks that calls from another queue are excluded from the fairness window.
The new public __invoke has no PHPDoc even though conventions.md:102 requires it for touched public methods, while the private helpers are documented.
The status/called_at/called_by_user_id transition duplicates Ticket::call() (task.md:5-6) instead of reusing that existing domain primitive after the waiting re-check.

review.summary: The change adds the CallNextTicket action, CallMode enum and NoWaitingTicketsException with deterministic ordering, the 3-ticket fairness rule, transactional queue/candidate locking, tests and synchronized docs. It meets the contract and almost all rules; the main gaps are a fairness fallback race when the only waiting normal is taken concurrently, missing tests for the concurrent skip path and cross-mode fairness history, and a couple of small convention/reuse nits. It is approvable after minor follow-ups.
